title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing + padding-minimization heuristics (v8)
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: reduce wasted tokens and improve throughput by grouping requests by sequence-length distributions while preserving latency SLOs and KV-cache locality. This PR implements a sequencelength-aware bucketing layer and padding-minimization heuristics inside the continuous batching scheduler, extends the kernel selector to prefer kernels that better amortize padding costs, and hardens KV cache access for concurrent batch assembly. Changes include heuristics for dynamic bucket sizing, max-pad thresholds, delayed dispatch for small outliers, and metrics/tracing for padding overheads. The description below contains the implementation summary, perf results, testing/QA checklist, and rollout plan. Implementation summary: - Scheduler: add SeqlenBucketer (configurable bucket boundaries and adaptive rebalancing based on observed seqlen histogram). Integrates with ContinuousBatcher to prefer forming batches within same bucket and optionally wait up to bucket_wait_ms to reduce padding. - Padding heuristics: compute optimal pad target per-batch using pctile (config) and max_pad_limit; introduce max_pad_tokens and pad_cost_estimate to decide immediate dispatch vs waiting. - Kernel selection: kernel_selector now exposes get_cost_estimate(model, seqlen, pad_target) to pick kernels that minimize walltime given padded lengths (improves choice between multihead-optimized and tiled kernels). - KV cache: fixed a race in kv_cache append during batch assembly (lock striping -> atomic reservation), added reference-counted shards to reduce contention for common prefixes. - Metrics & tracing: new metrics runtime.batch_padding_tokens, runtime.batch_padding_pct, runtime.bucket_wait_ms, runtime.kernel_choice, and tracing spans for bucket decision path. - Tests & docs: unit tests for bucketer and heuristics, integration perf canary, updated docs/perf/dynamic-batching.md with recommended config. Perf summary: On standard load shape (mix of short/medium/long prompts from benchmark-lab), end-to-end token throughput improved by 8-15% for GPU A100 inference with mixed sequence distribution; median latency unchanged for p95 targets, average padded tokens per-batch reduced ~10%. See benchmarks/perf/dynbatch_seqlen_bench.py for methodology and results. Rollout: feature-gated behind runtime.feature.dynamic_seqlen_bucketing; rollout to canary pool for 48h with perf regression monitor, then 1% -> 10% -> 100% traffic over 7 days. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for SeqlenBucketer and pad heuristics - [x] Integration perf canary script and baseline - [x] KV cache race fix + tests - [x] Metrics + dashboard PR prepared - [x] Docs updated - [x] Backwards compatible defaults (feature off by default) Related: ENG-1423 (dynamic batching roadmap), ENG-1980 (kv-cache contention profiling).

review_comments: Liam: Can you justify the bucket_wait_ms default? It seems risky for p95. Please add test for tail latency under bursty arrival.
Aisha: Added a perf test (tests/integration/test_dynbatch_endtoend.py) that simulates bursty arrivals; default bucket_wait_ms=5ms is tuned to keep p95 within SLO for our canary workloads.
Marina: Race in kv_cache found during local stress — please use fine-grained locks or atomic reservations instead of a global lock. Also add a metric for kv_cache contention.
Aisha: Reworked kv_cache: introduced atomic reservation per-shard and refcounted shards to reduce contention. Added runtime.kv_cache_contended_count metric.
Rahul: Kernel selector change looks good; add comment about fallback to legacy selector for legacy configs. Also please add unit test for cost function edge cases.
Aisha: Added fallback path and unit tests for cost function; clarified comments and included microbench. Approving pending CI.
CI: First run failed on flaky test tests/unit/test_seqlen_bucketer.rs (timing-sensitive). Replaced timeouts with mocks and re-ran. CI passes.
ci_details: perf-canary: pass (no regressions; +10% throughput observed on mix)
release_notes: Improved dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics reduce average padded tokens and improve throughput. Added kernel selection cost estimates, KV cache contention fixes, and observability for padding overheads. Feature gated behind runtime.feature.dynamic_seqlen_bucketing.
notes_for_ops: Feature disabled by default. Enable via runtime config: feature.dynamic_seqlen_bucketing=true. Monitor metrics runtime.batch_padding_pct and runtime.kv_cache_contended_count during rollout. Canary script located at benchmarks/perf/dynbatch_seqlen_bench.py. Rollback: flip feature flag off to return to previous behavior.
changelog_entry: Runtime: Add sequence-length-aware bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics to continuous batching (feature-gated). Performance: ~8-15% throughput improvement on mixed-seq workloads; ~10% reduction in padded tokens.
notes: No backward-incompatible API changes. Configs added with sane defaults; customers can opt-in. Observability dashboard PR: redwood/observability-pack#1247 prepared by Dima.
